title: ceil
summary: Round values toward positive infinity in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Falls back to the host implementation when the active provider lacks unary_ceil.

description: `ceil(X)` rounds each element of `X` toward positive infinity, returning the smallest integer greater than or equal to each value. Real integer inputs preserve their exact class, shape, and values.
behaviors: Works on scalars, vectors, matrices, and higher-dimensional tensors with MATLAB broadcasting semantics.
All eight real integer classes are exact identity operations and preserve class on host, in tables or timetables, and on supported resident providers.
Logical inputs are promoted to doubles (`false → 0`, `true → 1`) before applying the ceiling operation.
Character arrays are interpreted numerically (their Unicode code points) and return dense double tensors.
Complex inputs are rounded component-wise: `ceil(a + bi) = ceil(a) + i·ceil(b)`.
Empty arrays return empty arrays of the appropriate shape.
GPU integer input retains the same exact resident handle; floating and logical provider fallback restores output residency after host evaluation.

faqs.question: Does `ceil` always round toward positive infinity?
faqs.answer: Yes—positive values round up away from zero, while negative values round toward zero (e.g., `ceil(-0.1) = 0`).

faqs.question: How are complex numbers handled?
faqs.answer: The real and imaginary parts are ceiled independently, matching MATLAB's component-wise definition.

faqs.question: What happens with logical arrays?
faqs.answer: Logical values promote to doubles (`0` or `1`) before rounding, so the outputs remain 0 or 1.

faqs.question: Can I pass character arrays to `ceil`?
faqs.answer: Yes. Character data is treated as its numeric code points, producing a double tensor of the same size.

faqs.question: Will GPU execution change floating-point results?
faqs.answer: No. Providers implement IEEE-compliant ceiling; when a provider lacks `unary_ceil`, RunMat falls back to the CPU to preserve MATLAB-compatible behaviour.

faqs.question: Can fusion keep `ceil` on the GPU?
faqs.answer: Yes. `ceil` participates in elementwise fusion, so fused graphs can stay resident on the device when supported.

gpu_behavior: When tensors already reside on the GPU, exact integer input is returned as the same resident handle because every value is already integral. Floating and logical input uses the provider `unary_ceil` hook when available; otherwise RunMat gathers once, applies the host operation, and re-uploads to the owning provider.
